summary: Walking-skeleton rustia VM spike: measure rustia OWN us/decision on grabby AI kernel (native + wasm-in-V8) vs the 0.73us reference-Luau bar; parallel gc-arena Send/serde/steppable micro-spike; then adversarial verification of the numbers against on-disk artifacts

skeleton.summary: Built a from-scratch register-bytecode VM ("rustia walking-skeleton") and benched it on the EXACT grabby AI kernel/harness shape (mirroring spike-a-luau + ai_bakeoff lib.rs/koto_path.rs). Result: the VM hits the Luau-class bar on BOTH native and wasm. Realistic path (IAUS argmax in VM bytecode, eps-greedy/SARSA(lambda)/contagion in Rust, exactly like spike-A's tick_luau_realistic) = ~0.93 us/decision native, ~0.99 us/decision wasm32-in-V8. The native floor anchor reproduced 0.147 us/d (validates the harness vs the 0.149 target), and the TIER-2 Q16.16 VM path reproduced the golden AI hash 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 bit-identically on native AND wasm (node + deno). Deterministic per-instruction fuel is essentially free (0-3%). Full-VM wasm tax is only ~1.06-1.09x (no extra tax beyond what pure Rust pays). rustia sits ~4-6x faster than koto (4.0/5.9) and within the 0.7-1.5us Luau band, ~1.27x slower than the Luau-realistic 0.73 reference — a gap the design's planned-but-unimplemented fused-product superinstruction closes (320 dispatches/argmax-call is ~3x more than an optimized encoding needs). Verdict: GO.
skeleton.design_implemented: VALUE REPR: real NaN-boxed 8-byte Value (struct Value(u64)). Numbers = inline f64 (is_num = (bits & QNAN)!=QNAN, where QNAN=0x7ffc000000000000); tagged values live in the quiet-NaN range: low-3-bit discriminator 1=nil/2=false/3=true/4=int with i32 payload at bits[3..35) (encode QNAN|4|((i as u32)<<3), decode ((bits>>3) as u32) as i32); heap handle = SIGN|QNAN|48-bit (defined, NOT exercised — kernel is pure scalar). Mask/shift is genuinely paid on every type check (truthy/is_num) and every int box/unbox; for numbers the decode is from_bits (the honest NaN-box cost, which is the type-check branches, not a per-op mask). Canonicalizing num_canon (NaN->fixed qNaN, -0.0->+0.0) exists but is kept OFF the f64 perf path to stay apples-to-apples with Luau/koto-float; the determinism path is integer Q16 so needs no float canonicalization. OPCODE SET (~24): LOADK, MOVE, NADD/NSUB/NMUL/NDIV/NMOD/NMODK/NMULK (f64), NLT/NLE/NEQ/NEQK (f64 compare->bool), FORNPREP/FORNLOOP (numeric-for superinstruction over reg[a],a+1,a+2), AGET (computed array index), JMP/JMPIF/JMPIFNOT, RET, ILT/IEQ (int), CALL (host fn: 0=fxmul (a*b)>>16, 1=curve_kind w/ logistic LUT). Fixed-width 8-byte instr {op:u8,a,b,c,aux:i32} decoded straight in the loop (no two-level decode). DISPATCH: ONE big `match i.op` inside `loop` (lowers to jump-table native / br_table wasm). FUEL: const-generic `run<const FUEL:bool>` — when on, decrement budget + trap-check each dispatched op; measured cost ~0-3% (essentially free). SUPERINSTRUCTIONS: numeric-FOR (FORNPREP/FORNLOOP) implemented and used for both action(0..5) and consideration(0..3) loops; the fused IAUS PRODUCT/curve-MAC super-op is NOT implemented (the main identified headroom). KERNEL BYTECODE: NO Luau parser — produced by a ~40-line ad-hoc label-resolving assembler (Asm struct: emit/emit_j/emit_aux/label + 2-pass fixup), two programs hand-assembled: build_argmax_f64 (35 instrs, mirrors spike-A ARGMAX_SRC: kind0=x*x,kind1=x,kind2=1-x,*1.25 momentum, argmax) and build_argmax_q16 (27 instrs, mirrors grabby KotoSelector SCRIPT via host fxmul+curve).

skeleton.wasm_result: rustia VM realistic = 0.985-0.990 us/decision in node v25.8.1, 0.996-1.013 us/decision in deno 2.8.2 (both V8), vs 0.93-0.96 us/decision native -> full-VM wasm tax ~1.06x (node) / ~1.09x (deno). The native-floor anchor also pays ~1.09x in wasm (0.16 vs 0.147), so the VM dispatch loop incurs NO penalty beyond the baseline wasm tax that even branch-free pure Rust pays. This extends Spike B (dispatch-only ~parity) to a REAL VM with NaN-box memory access + register-file loads/stores + a contagion pass touching n*4 neighbor reads, and the big-match->br_table dispatch stays at ~parity. Checksums were bit-identical between node and deno for every path (e.g. realistic n=1000 = 0x-31fa8ccbfee14a97 in both), confirming cross-runtime determinism. wasm binary is 68 KB. Fuel ON vs OFF in wasm: 0.985 vs 0.957 (node), ~3% -> fuel essentially free in wasm too.
skeleton.determinism_result: MATCH (bit-identical), reproduced on THREE targets. TIER-2 implemented in full: the Q16.16 VM argmax (build_argmax_q16) uses host CALL ops for fxmul ((a*b)>>16) and curve_kind (the SAME libm-built logistic LUT + quadratic + inverse-linear as grabby), with loop control + momentum + argmax in bytecode; everything else in the tick (ChaCha8+fnv1a(id,tick) eps-greedy in the SAME RNG order as native, SARSA(lambda), input-drift, mood, snapshot-then-apply contagion) is Rust, identical to the native floor. Ran the golden config (n=4000, seed=0xA1BACE50, 200 ticks) and FNV-hashed AI state via the same state_hash. Produced hash = 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 on (1) native aarch64-mac, (2) wasm32-unknown-unknown in node v25, (3) wasm32-unknown-unknown in deno. Native floor in the same harness also = 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2. So the from-scratch VM's deterministic path is bit-equivalent to the native Q16.16 kernel and to grabby's pinned golden across native + wasm. (The REALISTIC f64 path is intentionally NOT hash-equivalent — it uses x*x instead of the logistic LUT, a perf proxy exactly like spike-A realistic / koto-float — and is excluded from the golden claim by design.)
skeleton.verdict: GO. A from-scratch Rust register-bytecode VM hits the Luau-class ~0.7-1.5us bar on BOTH native (0.93 us/decision) and wasm32-in-V8 (0.99 us/decision) on the real grabby IAUS argmax shape, ~4-6x faster than koto (4.0/5.9) and well within the band. The full-VM wasm tax is only ~1.06-1.09x with no penalty beyond baseline Rust, validating the portable big-match->br_table dispatch thesis at the level of a real VM (not just dispatch-only). The determinism contract holds: the Q16.16 VM path is bit-identical to grabby's golden 0x31c6ec2734ea6fa2 across native + wasm(node) + wasm(deno), and per-instruction deterministic fuel costs ~0%. The only gap to the Luau-realistic 0.73 reference (rustia is ~1.27x slower) is attributable to the naive skeleton encoding (320 dispatches/argmax-call, ~3x more than needed) lacking the fused-product/curve-MAC superinstruction the data-driven design already calls for — implementing it is expected to reach ~0.4-0.5us and beat Luau. The bar is hit today and beatable with the planned superinstructions.
caveats: Skeleton omits the fused IAUS PRODUCT / curve-MAC super-op and loop unrolling: only the numeric-FOR superinstruction is implemented, so 320 dispatches/argmax-call (~3x an optimized encoding). This is the entire reason rustia lands at 0.93 not <0.5, and the main path to beating Luau's 0.73.

The realistic comparison removes Luau's mlua FFI tax: rustia's realistic call is a direct in-process Rust call into the VM (legitimate, since rustia embeds without FFI), so the WORKLOAD is apples-to-apples with spike-A but rustia gets a structural call-overhead advantage. Even so, rustia's pure interpreter (0.82us/argmax-call) is somewhat slower than Luau's optimized bytecode interpreter; the gap is in the dispatch encoding, not the boundary.

The f64 realistic path is a perf proxy, NOT determinism-equivalent (uses x*x instead of the logistic LUT) — same design choice as spike-A realistic / koto-float. The golden-hash claim rests solely on the Q16.16 host-call path (proven). f64-realistic determinism is confirmed cross-RUNTIME (node==deno) but I did not assert native==wasm bit-equality for the f64 path (not the determinism contract).

No heap types exercised on the hot path: the NaN-box heap-handle tag is defined but unused. No tables, strings, metatables, closures, varargs, or GC — i.e. none of the Luau language surface or the gc-arena/Arc-clone cost centers koto pays. A real Luau-compat VM must add these; this skeleton only proves the SCALAR arithmetic/dispatch core.

Full 'vm-internal' (entire agent loop incl. SARSA(lambda)/drift/mood/contagion in bytecode) was DEFERRED. Rationale: unlike spike-A (where vm-internal mattered to amortize per-agent mlua FFI), rustia's realistic path has no FFI, so realistic already largely isolates VM cost; the isolation micro-bench (0.82us/argmax-call) gives the clean VM-only contribution. A true vm-internal would be strictly SLOWER (more bytecode) and is the conservative upper bound, not measured end-to-end.
No real Luau parser/compiler: bytecode hand-assembled via a tiny ad-hoc label-resolving assembler for JUST the kernel. Register file fixed at 24, local array at 8 — sized for this kernel only.

Single-threaded, single VM instance; Send/Sync and the 'N VMs on a thread pool' model are not exercised. opt-level 3 + LTO + codegen-units=1 + panic=abort; numbers are aarch64 M4 Max only (no x86_64-linux run here).

gcArena.summary: gc-arena micro-spike built against the LATEST gc-arena 0.6.0 (task said 0.5.x; 0.6.0 is current — Collect is now lifetime-parameterized `Collect<'gc>`, no serde feature exists). A 4-test spike compiles and runs at $HOME/.claude/jobs/d3f0d35e/tmp/spike-ga-gcarena. Verdict: VIABLE-WITH-CAVEATS. The Send gate FAILS by default (two precise causes) but a sound `unsafe impl Send` wrapper compiles, moves a live Gc object graph to a pool thread, and is used there successfully — matching exactly the move-whole-VM-to-a-thread model rustia needs (Send-not-Sync). Serde round-trips. Fuel-driven stepping works cleanly.
gcArena.send_result:
FAILS by default; FIXABLE with a sound wrapper. `fn assert_send<T:Send>(){}; assert_send::<Arena<Rootable![Root<'_>]>>()` does NOT compile. Exact compiler reasons (raw E0277, both fire):
(1) `NonNull<gc_arena::types::GcBoxInner<RefLock<Table<'static>>>>` cannot be sent between threads — i.e. the raw Gc pointers in the root object graph (`Gc<'gc,T>` wraps a `NonNull`, which is `!Send`).
(2) `Rc<metrics::MetricsInner>` inside `gc_arena::context::Context` (Box<Context> field of Arena) cannot be sent — the non-atomic refcount on the GC pacing metrics.
Neither is Sync-related; both are Send blockers. A `struct SendArena(MyArena); unsafe impl Send for SendArena {}` wrapper COMPILES, and `assert_send::<SendArena>()` passes. I then `std::thread::spawn(move || { arena.0.mutate(...) })` — moved the whole arena+graph to another thread and read the root table there: prints "root table len = 1". SOUNDNESS argument (documented in the spike): both blockers are arena-internal — Gc pointers are branded by the invariant 'gc and provably cannot escape `mutate`, and the only external clone of the metrics Rc comes from `Arena::metrics()`. If the embedding never retains a `Metrics` (or other arena-derived) handle across a thread boundary, moving the whole arena is a unique-owner move with no aliasing and no cross-thread refcount race. This is the same situation piccolo's !Send VM is in; the wrapper is the standard fix. Caveat: it is `unsafe` and rests on that one documented invariant (don't hand out long-lived metrics() clones to other threads).
gcArena.serde_result: WORKS, both directions, branded lifetime is only a mild obstacle in one direction. Read-OUT (the C4-relevant direction: script Value -> Rust struct via serde::Deserialize): needs only &-refs into the graph, NO Mutation, so the 'gc brand is a NON-issue — a `serde::Deserializer` over `&Value<'gc>` has the same trivial lifetime story as my `value_to_json(&Value)` walker. Demonstrated: serialized the live arena graph to JSON `{"inner":{"greeting":"hello","n":42.0}}`. Write-INTO-arena (deserialize external bytes -> fresh arena): the ONLY friction — allocating Gc needs `&Mutation<'gc>`, which std `Deserialize::deserialize` cannot thread through its signature. Idiomatic fix is a `serde::de::DeserializeSeed` carrying `&Mutation` (mechanical, ~30 lines for a Value type). I demonstrated the equivalent hand-written recursive builder `json_to_value(mc, &json)` running inside a fresh `Arena::new`, and asserted byte-identical round-trip (s == s2): "round trip identical: OK". Conclusion: serde bridge is fully feasible; the brand costs you one DeserializeSeed wrapper for the into-arena path only.
gcArena.steppable_result: WORKS — fuel-driven collection is exactly the supported model, no obstacle. The mutate-XOR-collect dance is enforced by the API shape: GC only happens in `collect_debt`/`finish_cycle`/`cycle_debt`, never inside `mutate` (the arena docs explicitly state "no garbage collection will take place during this method"). My stackless loop: 2000 steps, each does `arena.mutate(|mc,root| {alloc 10 transient Gc garbage; every 100th step push a retained Value})`, then at the step boundary `arena.metrics().adjust_debt(fuel_per_step)` + `arena.collect_debt()`. `Metrics::adjust_debt(f64)` lets you inject debt from YOUR fuel counter rather than relying on allocation pressure or wall-clock, so collection is fully deterministic w.r.t. the fuel schedule. Result: "2000000 fuel over 2000 steps; live retained = 20; total heap bytes ever = 448; gc cycles run = 10" — garbage was reclaimed (heap stayed tiny, 20 live values kept), 10 incremental cycles ran, all driven by my explicit calls. `finish_cycle()` gives a deterministic full-collection checkpoint at any chosen boundary. Stackless fits: the VM owns no Gc across the collect call (Gc cannot escape mutate), so there is nothing on a Rust stack to root — state lives in the arena root, which is exactly the stackless requirement.
gcArena.ergonomics: Honest assessment: the branded 'gc lifetime is a real, persistent tax but a well-trodden one (it is the piccolo embedding model). (a) HOST NATIVE FNS in/out: every value-touching signature carries 'gc — e.g. `fn(&Mutation<'gc>, &[Value<'gc>]) -> Value<'gc>`. Inside a `mutate` callback this is ergonomic (Gc<'gc,T> is Copy, derefs freely to &'gc T, NaN-boxed Value can stay Copy). The friction is that EVERY type that holds a Gc must `#[derive(Collect)] #[collect(no_drop)]` and cannot impl Drop, and host-owned leaf data (String, your LUTs) must be wrapped in `Static<T>` (T:'static) to satisfy Collect — minor but pervasive boilerplate. Values cannot be stored in plain Cell/RefCell; you must use the crate's `Lock`/`RefLock` + `unlock(mc)` to get write barriers right (I used RefLock for tables). (b) RE-ENTRANT / POLL-STYLE Sequence callbacks: this is where the tax bites — a Gc pointer CANNOT be held across a yield/step boundary because the arena may collect between steps and the 'gc brand differs per mutate call. gc-arena 0.6 ships the exact tool piccolo uses: `DynamicRootSet::stash(mc, gc) -> DynamicRoot<R>` (a 'static handle) and `.fetch(&root) -> Gc<'gc,...>` to re-root after resume. So re-entrant native callbacks are doable but pay a stash/fetch indirection (a slotmap lookup) per value carried across a suspension, plus the API ceremony of DynamicRoot handles. For rustia's stackless fuel VM this is acceptable: most work is inside one mutate; only true host-yield/await points need stashing. Net: moderate tax, front-loaded into the embedding-API design, not the hot interpreter loop.

gcArena.verdict: VIABLE-WITH-CAVEATS for rustia. The Send-only requirement is MET, but only via a sound `unsafe impl Send` wrapper around the Arena (gc-arena does NOT give you Send out of the box: blocked by `NonNull` Gc pointers and a non-atomic `Rc` in the metrics). The wrapper compiled, moved a live Gc graph to a pool thread, and ran mutate there — this is precisely the move-whole-VM-to-a-worker model, and it is the same pattern piccolo embedders use, so it is battle-tested rather than novel. Caveats to bake into the go decision: (1) the Send wrapper carries one documented invariant — the embedding must never hand a `metrics()` clone (or other arena-derived handle) to another thread; trivially satisfiable since we control the API. (2) serde: reading script values into Rust structs (C4) is free of lifetime pain; deserializing external data INTO the arena costs one DeserializeSeed wrapper threading &Mutation. (3) fuel-driven stepping is a first-class fit via adjust_debt + collect_debt/finish_cycle. (4) the branded 'gc lifetime imposes pervasive but shallow boilerplate (derive(Collect)/no_drop, Static<T> for host leaves, Lock/RefLock for mutability) and forces DynamicRootSet stash/fetch for any Gc carried across a re-entrant callback yield. Note the spec said 0.5.x but 0.6.0 is current and changes Collect to be lifetime-parameterized; plan against 0.6.0.

verify.honesty_check: REAL VM, no cheat detected. I read $HOME/.claude/jobs/d3f0d35e/tmp/spike-sk-rustia/src/lib.rs in full and re-ran a clean rebuild. (1) Big-match dispatch: Vm::run has ONE `match i.op {...}` (lib.rs:440-552) over ~24 opcodes inside `loop`, decoding fixed-width 8-byte Instr via get_unchecked(pc) — not constant folding. (2) Real bytecode: two hand-assembled programs via the Asm label-resolver — build_argmax_f64 (35 instrs, reported 320 dispatches/call) mirrors spike-A ARGMAX_SRC (kind0=x*x/kind1=x/kind2=1-x, *1.25 momentum, argmax), build_argmax_q16 (27 instrs, 219 dispatches) mirrors grabby KotoSelector via host CALL fxmul/curve. Verified line-by-line against /workspace/src/rustia/spikes/spike-a-luau/src/main.rs and the grabby Q16.16 kernel embedded in lib.rs (fx_mul, logistic LUT, fnv1a, learn/contagion all verbatim). (3) Real NaN-box: Value(u64) with genuine bit ops — is_num = (bits&QNAN)!=QNAN, truthy = tag compares, int encode QNAN|4|((i as u32)<<3) / decode (bits>>3) (lib.rs:114-164). Not secretly an f64. (4) Per-instruction fuel: const-generic run<const FUEL:bool>, decrement+trap each dispatch (lib.rs:431-438); fuel-OFF path measured separately. (5) Data-dependent: World::new seeds inputs+neighbors via ChaCha8Rng (lib.rs:728); each tick reseeds per agent via fnv1a(i,tick) (lib.rs:840), marshals THAT agent's inputs into arr[] fresh before each VM run, contagion touches n*4 neighbor reads. Isolation bench rotates arr by (w&63) so it can't fold (main.rs:88-106). black_box guards state_hash/acc/sink (main.rs:18,108,122). state_hash mixes all q/trace/last_action/mood. Nothing is dead-code-eliminated.

verify.gc_arena_verdict: Independently CONFIRMED by compiling $HOME/.claude/jobs/d3f0d35e/tmp/spike-ga-gcarena (gc-arena 0.6.0 pinned in Cargo.lock; task spec said 0.5.x). Arena: Send does NOT hold by default: `cargo build --release --features prove_not_send` (which enables assert_send::<MyArena>()) FAILS to compile with E0277, citing exactly the two claimed causes — (1) NonNull<GcBoxInner<RefLock<Table>>> (the Gc raw pointers) is !Send, and (2) Rc<metrics::MetricsInner> inside Context is !Send (non-atomic refcount) — plus a third same-family NonNull<GcBoxInner<()>> from Context. The default build (SendArena wrapper with `unsafe impl Send`) compiles, `assert_send::<SendArena>()` passes, and at runtime it MOVES a live Gc graph to a std::thread::spawn pool thread and reads it there ("[SEND] moved arena to pool thread; root table len = 1"). So: raw Arena is !Send, but the documented unsafe wrapper makes it Send and the move-whole-VM-to-a-worker model works — matching the report's "VIABLE-WITH-CAVEATS / FAILS by default, FIXABLE with sound wrapper" exactly. Serde round-trip ([SERDE] round trip identical: OK) and fuel-driven stepping (2000000 fuel, 20 live retained, 448 bytes, 10 gc cycles, explicit finish_cycle) also reproduced. Caveat the report itself states: the wrapper's safety is an argument (never hand a metrics() clone across threads), not a compiler proof — but it is the standard piccolo pattern.

The summary's actual ~1.06-1.09x 'full-VM wasm tax' claim is realistic-wasm / realistic-NATIVE (0.96/0.93), which is the correct apples-to-apples and is sound (I reproduce ~1.03-1.04x).
